title: Durga, Kali, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Parvati as characters

segments.voice: Yesterday closed the reading of the Devi Mahatmya, the goddess text read from start to finish. Which scene stayed with you? Today the goddess steps out of one book and into many stories. Day one thousand seventy-two.

A woman stands at a window, watching the road. A year has gone by since her daughter married and moved far away, up into the mountains, to a husband who smears himself with ash and has no house to speak of. Now autumn is here, and the daughter is coming home for a few days, bringing the children. The mother has been cooking since morning. That woman is Menaka, queen of the mountains, in songs people sing in Bengal. And the daughter she's waiting for rides a lion. Today the path starts a new stretch: five goddesses, met not as titles, but as characters.
screen: `A MOTHER AT A WINDOW.` → `A DAUGHTER COMING HOME.` → `THE DAUGHTER RIDES A LION.`

segments.voice: Durga, Kali, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Parvati. Over the next days this path takes them one at a time, the way you'd get to know people: what they do, who they love, what makes them angry, what they choose. Some Hindus hear all five as faces of one great Goddess, the way the Devi Mahatmya's goddesses all walked back into one. Others hold one of them close as their own. This path will tell the stories and leave that to each family. Start with Durga. In the Devi Mahatmya she is the one the gods can't do without. When the buffalo demon has beaten them, their combined radiance becomes her, and each god hands her a weapon. She laughs in battle. She doesn't need rescuing. She is the rescue. But in Bengal, at Durga Puja, the same goddess is also somebody's daughter. Tradition there says she is Uma, born to the mountain king and queen, married to Shiva, and once a year she comes home to her parents. There are old songs, called agamani, sung in her mother's voice: the waiting, the worry, the joy at the gate. And when the festival ends, there are songs of farewell, as the image is carried to the water, and people say goodbye the way a family says goodbye to a married daughter going back to her husband's house. So one goddess holds two pictures at once. The warrior with a weapon in every hand. And the girl whose mother has been at the window all morning. Neither cancels the other. That's what it means to meet her as a character: she's more than one thing, and the stories let her be.
screen: `FIVE GODDESSES, MET AS CHARACTERS.` · `DURGA, THE ONE THE GODS CAN'T DO WITHOUT.` · `DURGA, A DAUGHTER COMING HOME.` · then, large: `ONE GODDESS, TWO PICTURES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: two pictures, held together. Sit, and let the breath slow. First, bring to mind someone strong in your life, someone who shows up when things are falling apart. Let their strength be there for a few breaths. Then see that same person somewhere soft: at a kitchen table, laughing, being fussed over, being somebody's child. Don't choose between the pictures. Let both be true. If you pray, you can bring that person before the Goddess in your own words. If you don't, just hold them, both ways at once. The bell holds the time.
Durga. The goddess the gods couldn't do without, and in Bengal's songs, a daughter coming home. The first of five characters. Today's word.

Your line: Durga, Kali, Lakshmi, Saraswati, Parvati as characters. Today, notice one person who is strong in one room and tender in another, and let them be both. Tomorrow, Kali. Day one thousand seventy-two.

howItsDone: In Bengal, Durga Puja is kept as both a celebration of the goddess's victory and a homecoming: families welcome Durga as a married daughter visiting her parents, and on the last day the clay images are carried to a river or pond for immersion.

fork.setup: you're Menaka, queen of the mountains. your daughter married an ash-covered ascetic and moved away. autumn comes. what do the songs show you doing?
options: forgetting her, since she's married now
waiting at the window, watching the road
sending soldiers to bring her back
fork.reveal: the agamani songs are sung in the mother's voice: the waiting, the worry, and the joy when the daughter comes home with her children.

original.note: Sanskrit: Durga. In the Devi Mahatmya's eleventh chapter, the goddess says she will take this name after slaying a demon called Durgama.

trapdoor: what you thought: Durga is a warrior goddess, and that's all.
what it means: in the Devi Mahatmya she's the gods' last hope; in Bengal she's also a daughter coming home.
what a scholar hears: Bengal's agamani and vijaya songs, sung in Menaka's voice, cast the goddess as Uma, the married daughter of the mountain king.
